Post-fix the same payload is rejected cleanly: ``` REJECTED CLEANLY: format() output exceeds the maximum of 1048576 bytes ``` ## Changes - `MAX_FORMAT_OUTPUT_BYTES = 1 MiB` enforced at every append in `format_args` (template segments, argument renders, and escaped braces), via a small `push_capped` helper. - New `ExpressionError::FormatOutputTooLarge`. 1 MiB is ~6 orders of magnitude above real workflow usage, so no legitimate expression changes behavior. # Pull Request #143: feat: CI gate + auto-PR after successful CI State: OPEN Draft: false Author: @Bnjoroge1 Base: main Head: Bnjoroge/ci-gate-auto-pr Merge state: DIRTY Created: 2026-08-16T23:44:57Z Updated: 2026-08-18T03:20:18Z URL: https://github.com/preloopdev/preloop/pull/143 ## Body Three complementary flows for opening a PR on GitHub after CI passes on preloop: 1. Webhook auto-PR (server github_pr.rs): when a push-triggered run succeeds, server opens a PR per policy (auto: feature/always/never, draft, exclude patterns). Commit-message labels [no-pr]/[draft]/[pr] override policy. Dedup against existing open PRs. Best-effort async. 2. Dirty-tree flow (CLI + server): preloop run on uncommitted changes runs CI on the server snapshot. After green, interactive prompt [y/N/d] (or labels/flags) decides whether to materialize a real commit from the tested tree, push, and open a PR via push endpoint. Server accepts optional {create_pr, draft} override on push. Branch-head fallback for verification. Author = dev git identity. 3. Pre-push hook (contrib/): soft CI gate for committed pushes. Holds git push open while CI runs. [skip ci] bypass, resumable cache, fail-open when unreachable. Also: snapshot-tree exposure, dirty submission relaxed validation, config types, 8 new tests. just test-ci green. ## What & why ## Protocol surface - [ ] I confirm this change touches the runner protocol interface: **YES / NO** ## Required gates - [ ] `just test-ci` passes locally (fmt-check + clippy `-D` + full test suite + runner-watch conformance) - [ ] If protocol/wire shapes changed: the change is validated against the official runner (golden replay via `runner-watch`, or a live capture showing the official bytes), not only unit tests - [ ] If the touched subsystem has property tests (`concurrency_properties`, scheduling, matrix expansion, …): they are extended for the changed contract and pass (`PROPTEST_CASES=256 cargo test -p preloop-runner-server`) - [ ] New wire fields/events are additive and serde-defaulted where the official runner would not send them - [ ] No secrets, credentials, or internal/deployment-specific paths are introduced (captures with live tokens must be redacted or excluded) ## Verification performed ## Checklist - [ ] Tests added/updated for any new observable contract - [ ] Docs updated (`docs/`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`) where behavior changed - [ ] Changelog-worthy user-facing change described in the PR body --- ## Summary by cubic Auto-opens GitHub PRs after green CI on push-triggered runs and adds a pre-push CI gate. Previously only clean-tree `preloop run --push --create-pr` could open PRs; now webhook push runs can open PRs per policy, and the gate prevents pushing red commits while failing open only on engine outages. - Server auto-PR: Runs from native GitHub push webhooks open a PR per policy (`feature|never`), defaulting to draft, with anchored branch-exclude patterns; head-commit labels `[no-pr]`, `[draft]`, and `[pr]` override. It deduplicates existing open PRs, URL-encodes queries, skips local repos, and fires once at run finalization. Strict env parsing backs config, and recent hardening enforces provenance. - Push endpoint and dirty-tree correctness: `POST /api/v1/runs/:run_id/push` optionally accepts `{ "create_pr": bool, "draft": bool }` overrides; non-boolean values are rejected. For dirty submissions, the server records the snapshot `tree_sha` at accept, rejects runs without one, verifies the pushed branch head matches the tested tree, records `effective_sha` for webhook dedup, and skips submit-time checks for dirty pushes. - CLI and pre-push hook: `--push` accepts dirty trees, materializes the tested commit once before retries using the developer’s git identity, runs non-interactively when explicit, and the prompt reports CI outcome. The embedded pre-push hook gates only (never pushes), chains any previous hook, respects `core.hooksPath`, caches per remote/endpoint/sha with run-id resume, bypasses `[skip ci]`, handles all-zero remote SHAs, and fails open only on the `PRELOOP_UNREACHABLE` marker. Docs in docs/ci-gate-auto-pr.md; tests cover auto-PR, dedup, dirty-tree verification, webhook dedup, and hook lifecycle. **Rollout / migration** - Grant the GitHub App `pull_requests: write`. - Set policy: `PRELOOP_GITHUB_PR_AUTO=feature|never`, `PRELOOP_GITHUB_PR_DRAFT=true|false`, `PRELOOP_GITHUB_PR_EXCLUDE=pattern1,pattern2`. If you used `always`, replace it with `feature`. - The pre-push gate auto-offers on first interactive `preloop run`; to install manually: `cp contrib/pre-push .git/hooks/pre-push && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-push`. Written for commit 55119f481736e7dea6dbd1aab8f9525fd9b11265. # Pull Request #143: feat: CI gate + auto-PR after successful CI State: OPEN Draft: false Author: @Bnjoroge1 Base: main Head: Bnjoroge/ci-gate-auto-pr Merge state: UNKNOWN Created: 2026-08-16T23:44:57Z Updated: 2026-08-18T03:20:18Z URL: https://github.com/preloopdev/preloop/pull/143 ## Body Three complementary flows for opening a PR on GitHub after CI passes on preloop: 1. Webhook auto-PR (server github_pr.rs): when a push-triggered run succeeds, server opens a PR per policy (auto: feature/always/never, draft, exclude patterns). Commit-message labels [no-pr]/[draft]/[pr] override policy. Dedup against existing open PRs. Best-effort async. 2. Dirty-tree flow (CLI + server): preloop run on uncommitted changes runs CI on the server snapshot. After green, interactive prompt [y/N/d] (or labels/flags) decides whether to materialize a real commit from the tested tree, push, and open a PR via push endpoint. Server accepts optional {create_pr, draft} override on push. Branch-head fallback for verification. Author = dev git identity. 3. Pre-push hook (contrib/): soft CI gate for committed pushes. Holds git push open while CI runs. [skip ci] bypass, resumable cache, fail-open when unreachable. Also: snapshot-tree exposure, dirty submission relaxed validation, config types, 8 new tests. just test-ci green. ## What & why ## Protocol surface - [ ] I confirm this change touches the runner protocol interface: **YES / NO** ## Required gates - [ ] `just test-ci` passes locally (fmt-check + clippy `-D` + full test suite + runner-watch conformance) - [ ] If protocol/wire shapes changed: the change is validated against the official runner (golden replay via `runner-watch`, or a live capture showing the official bytes), not only unit tests - [ ] If the touched subsystem has property tests (`concurrency_properties`, scheduling, matrix expansion, …): they are extended for the changed contract and pass (`PROPTEST_CASES=256 cargo test -p preloop-runner-server`) - [ ] New wire fields/events are additive and serde-defaulted where the official runner would not send them - [ ] No secrets, credentials, or internal/deployment-specific paths are introduced (captures with live tokens must be redacted or excluded) ## Verification performed ## Checklist - [ ] Tests added/updated for any new observable contract - [ ] Docs updated (`docs/`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`) where behavior changed - [ ] Changelog-worthy user-facing change described in the PR body --- ## Summary by cubic Auto-opens GitHub PRs after green CI on push-triggered runs and adds a pre-push CI gate. Previously only clean-tree `preloop run --push --create-pr` could open PRs; now webhook push runs can open PRs per policy, and the gate prevents pushing red commits while failing open only on engine outages. - Server auto-PR: Runs from native GitHub push webhooks open a PR per policy (`feature|never`), defaulting to draft, with anchored branch-exclude patterns; head-commit labels `[no-pr]`, `[draft]`, and `[pr]` override. It deduplicates existing open PRs, URL-encodes queries, skips local repos, and fires once at run finalization. Strict env parsing backs config, and recent hardening enforces provenance. - Push endpoint and dirty-tree correctness: `POST /api/v1/runs/:run_id/push` optionally accepts `{ "create_pr": bool, "draft": bool }` overrides; non-boolean values are rejected. For dirty submissions, the server records the snapshot `tree_sha` at accept, rejects runs without one, verifies the pushed branch head matches the tested tree, records `effective_sha` for webhook dedup, and skips submit-time checks for dirty pushes. - CLI and pre-push hook: `--push` accepts dirty trees, materializes the tested commit once before retries using the developer’s git identity, runs non-interactively when explicit, and the prompt reports CI outcome. The embedded pre-push hook gates only (never pushes), chains any previous hook, respects `core.hooksPath`, caches per remote/endpoint/sha with run-id resume, bypasses `[skip ci]`, handles all-zero remote SHAs, and fails open only on the `PRELOOP_UNREACHABLE` marker. Docs in docs/ci-gate-auto-pr.md; tests cover auto-PR, dedup, dirty-tree verification, webhook dedup, and hook lifecycle. **Rollout / migration** - Grant the GitHub App `pull_requests: write`. - Set policy: `PRELOOP_GITHUB_PR_AUTO=feature|never`, `PRELOOP_GITHUB_PR_DRAFT=true|false`, `PRELOOP_GITHUB_PR_EXCLUDE=pattern1,pattern2`. If you used `always`, replace it with `feature`. - The pre-push gate auto-offers on first interactive `preloop run`; to install manually: `cp contrib/pre-push .git/hooks/pre-push && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-push`. Written for commit 55119f481736e7dea6dbd1aab8f9525fd9b11265. name: ci
permissions:
  contents: read

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    # Keep push-triggered checks observable while the self-hosted pool boots.
  pull_request:
    # Docs-only PRs must not burn pool time: skip when every changed file
    # is a markdown document.
    paths-ignore:
      - "**/*.md"
  schedule:
    # Nightly intensive property profile at 02:00 UTC
    - cron: "0 2 * * *"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      profile:
        description: "Property profile: fast (default) or intensive"
        required: false
        default: "fast"


# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Property-test CI notes
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# PR / push: fast profile — 256 cases for pure/model/runner, 64 for HTTP.
# Scheduled / manual intensive: release mode, 10k cases, 100k shrink iters.
#
# The regular Linux jobs never run live GitHub or privileged official-runner
# probes. `runner-conformance.yml` runs the privileged deep runner probe on the
# dedicated smolVM self-hosted pool for every pull request.
# The differential harness dry-run (credential-free) runs in both profiles.
#
# Sleep-guard: each property-test job mechanically scans new test files for
# `sleep(` and fails the build if any match is found.
#
# Zero-filter guard: `cargo test -- --list | grep <filter>` must return at
# least one test name before case-count runs are launched.
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

jobs:
  rust:
    # Runs on the preloop self-hosted pool: the product's own runner is the
    # CI executor (dogfood).
    runs-on: self-hosted
    timeout-minutes: 60
    env:
      # 2 parallel debug rustc + GNU ld links peak ~4.6 GiB in the guest
      # (measured on the pool, 2026-08-13); the 5 GiB VM ceiling is the
      # floor. Unbounded parallelism OOM-killed the host once; the ceiling
      # must stay above the build peak or the guest OOM-kills rustc.
      CARGO_BUILD_JOBS: "2"
      # The dedicated property job carries the 256-case profile. Keep this
      # workspace gate aligned with `just test-ci` and bound libtest
      # concurrency so the dogfood VM survives preloop-runner's suite.
      PROPTEST_CASES: "8"
      RUST_TEST_THREADS: "2"
      RUSTFLAGS: "-C link-arg=-fuse-ld=lld"
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@08c6903cd8c0fde910a37f88322edcfb5dd907a8 # v5.0.0
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          # Conformance goldens are LFS-tracked; without this they arrive
          # as pointer stubs and every test that reads them fails.
          lfs: true
      - name: Materialize conformance goldens
        run: |
          git lfs pull --include=".runner-watch/golden/**"
          fixture=".runner-watch/golden/v2.335.1/06-multi-step/flows.jsonl"
          test -s "$fixture"
          if grep -q '^version https://git-lfs.github.com/spec/' "$fixture"; then
            echo "LFS fixture was not materialized: $fixture" >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@4360b52568e2003a75bf9bc1d59f33a8e3fc893c
        with:
          toolchain: "1.97"
          components: rustfmt,clippy

      # inline run steps work against preloop
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@49a0bdc70d2e1b713ca9e2869b211fcce03d3c1c

      # Runner executes as root in the pool VM; sudo's audit plugin fails on
      # the mis-owned /etc/sudoers in the golden, so call apt directly.
      - name: Install lld linker
        run: apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends lld

      - run: cargo fmt --all --check
      - run: |
          # Run clippy on warning-free crates with strict -D warnings
          cargo clippy --locked -p preloop-gha-protocol -p preloop-gha-parser -p preloop-gha-expressions -p preloop-cache -p preloop-artifacts -p runner-watch -p preloop-conformance --all-targets -- -D warnings
          # Run clippy on crates with pre-existing warnings without -D warnings
          cargo clippy --locked -p preloop-runner -p preloop-runner-server -p preloop-runner-client -p preloop-dap --all-targets
      # cargo test (libtest) measured faster than nextest on this pool:
      # nextest's per-test process model cost ~4 min of spawn overhead on
      # 1628 fast unit tests (exec 17.5-18.0 min vs libtest 13.4 across
      # -j2x2, -j2x1, and serial configs). Keep libtest.
      - run: cargo test --locked --workspace
        env:
          RUSTFLAGS: "-A warnings -C link-arg=-fuse-ld=lld"

  # Bounded property-test profile
  property-tests-fast:
    runs-on: self-hosted
    timeout-minutes: 30
    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@08c6903cd8c0fde910a37f88322edcfb5dd907a8 # v5.0.0
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          # Conformance goldens are LFS-tracked; without this they arrive
          # as pointer stubs and every test that reads them fails.
          lfs: true
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@4360b52568e2003a75bf9bc1d59f33a8e3fc893c
        with:
          toolchain: "1.97"

      # Zero-filter guard so just fail if no properties match the filter
      - name: Verify concurrency_properties filter matches at least one test
        run: |
          count=$(PROPTEST_CASES=1 cargo test -p preloop-runner-server -- --list 2>/dev/null | grep -c 'concurrency_properties' || true)
          if [ "$count" -eq 0 ]; then
            echo "ERROR: filter 'concurrency_properties' matched zero tests in preloop-runner-server" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "concurrency_properties: $count test(s) found"

      - name: Verify property filters match tests
        run: |
          server=$(PROPTEST_CASES=1 cargo test -p preloop-runner-server -- --list 2>/dev/null | grep -Ec 'concurrency::properties|concurrency_properties|concurrency_http_properties' || true)
          runner=$(cargo test -p preloop-runner -- --list 2>/dev/null | grep -c 'timespan_tests' || true)
          parser=$(cargo test -p preloop-gha-parser -- --list 2>/dev/null | grep -c 'concurrency_' || true)
          if [ "$server" -eq 0 ] || [ "$runner" -eq 0 ] || [ "$parser" -eq 0 ]; then
            echo "ERROR: zero matching tests (server=$server runner=$runner parser=$parser)" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
      - name: Check no sleep() in property test files
        run: |
          files="crates/preloop-runner-server/src/concurrency_properties.rs crates/preloop-runner-server/src/concurrency_http_properties.rs"
          bad=0
          for f in $files; do
            if [ -f "$f" ] && grep -q 'sleep(' "$f"; then
              echo "ERROR: sleep() found in $f" >&2
              bad=1
            fi
          done
          if [ "$bad" -ne 0 ]; then exit 1; fi
          echo "Sleep guard: OK"

      # Pure properties (256 cases)
      - name: Pure concurrency properties
        run: |
          PROPTEST_CASES=256 cargo test -p preloop-runner-server \
            'concurrency::properties' -- --test-threads=1
          PROPTEST_CASES=256 cargo test -p preloop-runner-server \
            concurrency_properties::pure -- --test-threads=1

      # Scheduler model properties (256 cases)
      - name: Scheduler model properties
        run: |
          PROPTEST_CASES=256 cargo test -p preloop-runner-server \
            concurrency_properties::state_machine -- --test-threads=1

      # Expression / parser properties (256 cases)
      - name: Expression and parser properties
        run: |
          PROPTEST_CASES=256 cargo test -p preloop-gha-expressions -- --test-threads=1
          cargo test -p preloop-gha-parser concurrency_ -- --test-threads=1

      # Runner dispatcher properties (256 cases)
      - name: Runner dispatcher properties
        run: |
          cargo test -p preloop-runner timespan_tests -- --test-threads=1

      # HTTP sequence properties (64 cases — heavier)
      - name: HTTP sequence properties
        run: |
          PROPTEST_CASES=64 cargo test -p preloop-runner-server \
            concurrency_http_properties -- --test-threads=1

      # Differential harness dry-run (credential-free)
      - name: Differential harness dry-run (schema + algebraic validation)
        run: |
          python3 benchmarks/real-world/run-concurrency-property-probes.py \
            --dry-run \
            --corpus benchmarks/real-world/concurrency-property-cases.json

      - name: Differential harness rejects contaminated fixture
        run: |
          set +e
          python3 benchmarks/real-world/run-concurrency-property-probes.py \
            --dry-run \
            --corpus benchmarks/real-world/fixtures/contaminated-case.json
          status=$?
          set -e
          if [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; then
            echo "ERROR: harness did not reject contaminated fixture (expected nonzero exit)" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "Contamination rejection: OK (exit $status)"

      # Upload regression seeds on failure
      - name: Upload proptest regressions
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02
        with:
          name: proptest-regressions-fast
          path: |
            crates/**/proptest-regressions/
          if-no-files-found: ignore

  # Intensive scheduled / manual profile
  property-tests-intensive:
    runs-on: self-hosted
    timeout-minutes: 120
    if: github.event_name == 'schedule' || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.event.inputs.profile == 'intensive')
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@08c6903cd8c0fde910a37f88322edcfb5dd907a8 # v5.0.0
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          # Conformance goldens are LFS-tracked; without this they arrive
          # as pointer stubs and every test that reads them fails.
          lfs: true
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@4360b52568e2003a75bf9bc1d59f33a8e3fc893c
        with:
          toolchain: "1.97"

      # Zero-filter guard
      - name: Verify concurrency_properties filter matches at least one test
        run: |
          count=$(PROPTEST_CASES=1 cargo test -p preloop-runner-server -- --list 2>/dev/null | grep -c 'concurrency_properties' || true)
          if [ "$count" -eq 0 ]; then
            echo "ERROR: filter 'concurrency_properties' matched zero tests" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
